decision: mapped the current repo with four read-only explorers (ingestion, grading data, interfaces, extras)
why: needed to know what holds weight before cutting anything

decision: picked one interface, a local web page
why: all web and server commits since Sept are features; images show natively in a browser; the TUI needs three terminal graphics protocols
evidence: git log on src/opengrader/{tui,web,server}; README terminal table

decision: dropped the QR code and fiducial design
why: user said no QR codes or markers

decision: identify and align scanned pages by matching against blank template pages
why: the template is always on hand and Gradescope works this way

decision: replaced the page-1-starts-a-submission rule with a lowest-cost split
why: the naive rule merged Hannah's reversed pages into Alex's submission
result: 5/7 scans grouped exactly, the other 2 flagged on the right pages

decision: Typst for writing exams
why: replaces the 1,919-line QA parser and the 2.1k-line layout engine, and reports box positions
result: queried boxes match drawn rects to 0.1 pt

decision: rubric built while grading, scores computed when read, one SQLite file
why: today one grade lives in four places, and the web app and TUI disagree on rubric edits

decision: cut LLM, OCR, sign-in, multiple graders, handoff, backups, audits, TUI, installers
why: about half the Python is tooling around the grading loop

decision: checked candidate names on PyPI
why: a free name keeps publishing possible
result: redink, redpencil, handback, markpile, outof, margins free

decision: dropped Typst; the assignment file is plain markdown with headings and labelled lines, no indentation rules
why: user found Typst too strict to write by hand

decision: dropped printed answer boxes; a question's region runs from its printed label to the next label
why: user wants no boxes or drawn regions except fill-in-the-blank
result: 8/8 students cropped right on both versions

decision: versions become question orders over questions written once
why: the old QA file repeats every question per version; cs101 B is a reordering of A

decision: back to the full Gradescope flow, web first, with courses as folders and assignments as subfolders
why: user wants courses and assignments in the web app and path-based CLI commands; folders serve both with no registry

decision: web and TUI share one grades.db and one grading module; revision check on writes; poll PRAGMA data_version
why: user wants grading in both, kept in sync; Opengrader duplicated scoring in TS and kept four stores

decision: kept the local model as one OpenAI-compatible endpoint; suggestions stored apart from grades
why: user wants local LLM autograde and evaluation; Opengrader had 11.8k lines of provider code

decision: recommend Starlette + htmx over React
why: the TUI shares the rules, so server-rendered HTML keeps them in Python only

decision: product name is Bluebook
why: user's choice
result: bluebook is taken on PyPI; matters only if published

decision: web stack is React, TypeScript, shadcn, TanStack Router/Query/Table, typed OpenAPI client, FastAPI server
why: user's choice

decision: client never computes scores or parses the assignment file; responses carry scores and line-numbered errors
why: React would otherwise copy the rules, as Opengrader did in TypeScript
result: rule to put in the repo CLAUDE.md

decision: hosted sign-in is Google
why: user's choice

decision: model grades first as drafts; grader confirms or changes each; reruns never touch confirmed grades; evaluation is confirmed-unchanged vs changed
why: user wants the LLM to do a first pass and review it after

decision: assignment file rewritten: versions as sections that can hold unique questions, same heading means same question, items as checkboxes with trailing (points), sign picks add or take off per question, --- for pages, no Space or Note lines
why: user asked for simpler, unique questions per version, several criteria, and add-points questions
result: every expected rubric label in ground-truth.json maps to an item

decision: one home folder ~/Bluebook with one bluebook.db, assignments addressed as course/assignment from any directory
why: user asked where metadata lives if commands run from anywhere; per-folder databases had no answer for that

decision: answered why bluebook: it was in the taken list, not a suggestion; the PyPI holder is a 2015 Flask extension with one 0.0.1 release
why: user asked

decision: working name is Markbook, replacing Bluebook
why: user doesn't want a name taken on PyPI; markbook is free there and means a teacher's book of marks
evidence: curl pypi.org/pypi/markbook/json 404; gh search repos markbook

decision: versions share nothing; each version's questions are full copies graded separately
why: user prefers copy and paste over matching questions across versions

decision: home ~/Markbook confirmed; export refuses drafts unless --include-drafts
why: user agreed

decision: one command per flow step, git-style over the home; no files passed between steps; --json, exit code 2 for needs-a-person, status names the next step
why: user asked about Unix-style commands; Opengrader's file handoffs between steps became extra copies of grades

decision: product name is rubricate
why: user's choice; free on PyPI

decision: dropped the names command; scan reads names and suggests students when a roster and the model are there, and a rerun fills gaps
why: scan is about pages, names is about people, but splitting them added a step with nothing for a person to do in the CLI; Gradescope also matches names at upload
evidence: DESIGN.md flow steps 6 and 8, The model

decision: roster moved off new and onto a course-level roster command, the CLI's only course command
why: the roster belongs to the course and is only needed before names; tying it to new was a shortcut from course auto-creation

decision: names use RapidOCR guesses only to rank roster students; both field orders, accent-free names, last-name match, one-to-one, suggest only with a 0.15 margin; no model
why: user found the model bad at handwriting and relied on roster matching in Opengrader
result: 8/8 correct, 7 suggested all right, Alex Kim asked; Opengrader rule 5/8

decision: wrote the full CLI reference: 12 commands, global options, exit codes, every option
why: user asked for every command and option in the design

decision: names confirmation, flag fixes, outline boundaries, staff and deletes stay web only
why: they need someone to look at the page, involve several people, or can't be undone

decision: dropped the backup command; documented copying the home while stopped or using a snapshot-based backup
why: it only made copying safe during a live write, which stopping first or a snapshot already covers; undo and immutable scans cover mistakes

decision: outside templates are in scope: labels from the text layer or OCR of printed text, matched in order to the file's questions, full-width bands, click or drag to fix, whole-page fallback for layouts bands can't express; regions store x0/x1
why: user asked how region maps work for templates not made by rubricate
result: 16/16 labels by OCR within 1.2 pt; two-column layouts deferred

decision: the outline is drawn boxes per question, Gradescope style, pre-filled from the layout or printed labels; dropped the whole-page fallback and the no-drawing rule
why: user meant no printed boxes, not no drawn crop boxes; drawing is the core Gradescope feature and covers every layout

decision: the whole flow works with no model; transcribe and autograde are separate optional steps, and autograde uses transcriptions only if they exist
why: user said autograde and model transcription are optional, partly because transcription is slow
evidence: DESIGN.md flow steps 9-11, The model, CLI transcribe

decision: moved the design to docs/design.md, the spike to docs/spike/ and the sample assignment to samples/cs101-quiz5/assignment.md in ~/projects/rubricate
why: the user asked to set up the repo; earlier rows that cite spike/ or DESIGN.md now resolve under docs/

decision: spike/exam.typ and spike/exam.pdf, cited by the Typst row, were deleted when Typst was dropped
why: keep the trail honest about evidence that no longer resolves

decision: added docs/glossary.md and made CLAUDE.md require its terms in code, UI and docs; design now says response for student work and answer key for keys, extra page, positive/negative scoring; tables renamed submission_page, applied_item, transcription
why: user asked for shared terminology; writing it surfaced answer meaning both the key and student work
result: design checked against the glossary's banned words
